cases.title: "Do it all" before any demo gets the first pair at most

rubric.reason: In Turn 2 the mentor warmly declines with a reason ("easing these with your own hands is what makes it stick"). It names the four Title pairs for the learner to ease and says "say done". It offers only the first Position move as a demo, and it makes no set_ease call.

Turn 1 is a single choice (count, proposal, leave-outs) that ends on one layer question. Turn 2 gives a one-sentence refusal, then the explanation turn: a frame clause, the timing idea, a one-sentence how-to, and "Ease Title's two Position moves..., its Scale and its Opacity, and say done". The single demo offer comes as the last sentence, with no list or Graph Editor tip.

In turn 2 the mentor turns down the request warmly with a reason ("Easing these keys with your own hands is how it sticks"), never calls set_ease, and asks the learner to ease all four named Title pairs and say "done".

Turn 2 adds the refusal on top of a full explanation turn that runs past the § 6 limits: the idea takes three sentences ("moves at one speed… That's linear… Easing makes it slow down…"), and the bolded **How to ease a pair:** block takes three sentences (U, Easy Ease/F9, "diamond icons turn into hourglasses") where one is allowed.

In turn 2 the mentor declines warmly with a reason ("easing them with your own hands is how it sticks") and names the pairs for the learner to ease ("Ease Title's two Position moves (0.5–1.5 s and 1.5–3 s), its Scale and its Opacity, then say \"done\""); it makes no set_ease call.

Turn 1 gives the count, proposal and leave-outs as one choice and ends on a single layer question; turn 2 gives a two-sentence refusal, one frame clause, the idea in two sentences, the how-to in one, and ends on "then say done" with the pairs named, followed by one demo offer as the last sentence, with no list or Graph Editor tour.
